simulationRules: Alternate history, 1 January 1938. Austria, Germany, Czechia and Slovakia are four independent sovereign states. Slovakia became independent in 1937, which is the scenario's explicit divergence from history. Germany seeks regional dominance; Austria defends its independence; Czechia relies on industry; Slovakia balances between its neighbours. There are no active or predetermined wars, annexations, occupations or territorial transfers. Diplomacy is textual unless a human QA operator deliberately issues an existing typed engine command. The deterministic economy engine owns every authoritative number and state transition. All authored economic values are synthetic development-test balance, not historical statistics. AI may discuss strategy but must never invent authoritative quantities or claim that an uncommitted state change occurred.
startingTimelineText: January 1938. Central Europe enters a tense alternate-history crisis. Slovakia has been independent since 1937 and now balances between Germany, Austria and Czechia. Germany presses for regional dominance, Austria protects its sovereignty, and Czechia trusts its industrial strength. All four states begin independent and at peace; no Anschluss, war, occupation or territorial transfer is scripted.
